accent-strong.note: Accent-strong — the interactive accent (links, active tab, sort chevrons, sliders, progress, selection controls). `--accent` below stays the quiet hover SURFACE it has always been; the two are different jobs.

background.note: ═══ Operis pastel-navy palette — light ═══ Muted navy, deliberately not royal/saturated/neon and never near-black. Ink is navy (#1D2735) rather than grey so text belongs to the palette. Status hues stay semantic (see the status block below) — an error must never read as "just more blue".

brand-sky.note: Operis brand ramp — theme-invariant (no .dark override). These replace Open Mercato's lime/yellow pair, which read as a different company's identity against a pastel-navy product: a neon lime-to-yellow sweep is the one thing on screen that cannot belong to this palette. The Operis ramp runs sky → lilac → violet, so a brand moment still lifts off the page but stays inside the product's temperature.

chart-1.note: Chart series — chroma pulled back from the stock ramp so a dashboard sits inside the calm palette instead of shouting over it. Hues are kept far apart because a series still has to be told from its neighbour. The default series leads with the navy family.

focus-ring-inner.note: Focus ring halo — navy at low alpha so the ring belongs to the palette rather than reading as a browser default.

font-body.note: Third-party components that theme themselves through their own custom properties rather than inheriting. MDXEditor's stylesheet sets `font-family: var(--font-body)` / `var(--font-mono)` on its editing surface and defines neither, so without these two lines its rich-text area is the one input in the product whose typeface depends on undefined-variable fallback behaviour. Binding them to the product faces makes it explicit. Theme-invariant, like the two faces they alias: a typeface does not change between light and dark.

font-geist-mono.light: "DM Mono", ui-monospace, "SFMono-Regular", "SF Mono", Consolas, "Liberation Mono", Menlo, monospace

font-geist-sans.note: Figtree / DM Mono are SELF-HOSTED — see ./fonts.css, imported at the top of this file. They are deliberately not pulled from fonts.googleapis.com: the app's CSP is `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` with no external hosts, so a Google Fonts <link> is blocked at runtime and the product would silently fall back to system type. The system stack stays behind them so an offline or blocked-font environment degrades to native type, never to a serif.

font-size-overline.note: ═══ Design System: Typography ═══ The scale is deliberately narrow. A page title is LIGHT (400) and large; weight is spent on the things that must be scanned — table headers, tabs, nav items — not on the heading, which already has size.

input-bg.note: Input family — text-entry chrome. A filled field takes `modal-muted` so a populated form reads at a glance without adding a border weight.

radius-sm.note: ═══ Design System: Radius Scale ═══ Explicit values rather than offsets from a single `--radius`, so each step is a decision instead of a side effect: sm = inline chips and checkboxes, md = compact buttons and menu items, lg = default controls (button, input, nav item), xl = cards, tables and popovers, 2xl = modals.

shadow-focus.note: Focus indicator — ONE mechanism for the whole product. The design reference suppresses focus rings entirely; we keep them (a keyboard user must be able to see where they are) but adopt the intent: quiet. A 2px ground-coloured inner ring separates the halo from the control, then a 4px navy halo at low alpha. Because it is a token, the whole app's focus treatment moves as one decision.

shadow-switch-thumb.note: Switch thumb: thin drop shadow + hairline outline (matches Figma switch spec).

shadow-xs.note: ═══ Design System: Shadow Scale ═══ Tuned to the navy ink #1D2735 so elevation reads as a cool shadow rather than a grey smudge over the pastel-navy surfaces. Dark overrides in .dark. xs → flat controls (button, input, icon-button) sm → cards, panels, sections md → the list-view card (a table carries elevation instead of a border) lg → menus, popovers, dropdowns xl → floating panels (drawers, side sheets) 2xl → top-level modals, command palette

sidebar.note: Sidebar — an inked chrome column, NOT a step on the neutral surface ladder. The rail is painted in the CTA navy (`--sidebar` == `--primary`) so the product's one saturated colour anchors the left edge, and every piece of nav chrome therefore has to read on navy rather than on white. That is why the family is complete — ink, quiet ink, hover fill, active pill, hairline — instead of borrowing `foreground` / `surface-muted` / `border` from the content side: those are tuned for a light ground and vanish here. `--sidebar-muted-foreground` is the quiet ink (rest-state icons, group overlines); the active row is a pale `--sidebar-primary` pill with `--sidebar-primary-foreground` ink, which reads as the rail colour cut out of the row.

status-error-bg.note: Error — muted brick red. Pulled back from the stock red-600 so a warning row does not shout across the pastel-navy chrome, while staying unmistakably red and AA-legible. `icon` tracks `--destructive` by design.

status-info-bg.note: Info — indigo-leaning blue, held one hue away from `--accent-strong` so an informational chip is never mistaken for an interactive element.

status-neutral-bg.note: Neutral — navy-grey rather than pure grey, so a "no status" chip reads as part of the palette instead of as an unstyled leftover.

status-pink-bg.note: Pink (hue ~340°) — a CATEGORICAL accent for stage/category chips, never a semantic outcome. Chroma pulled back to match the rest of the palette.

status-warning-bg.note: Warning — muted ochre. Amber is the hardest hue to keep legible on a light tint, so the icon sits deliberately darker than a stock amber-600.

table-header.note: Table family — a list view is the most-used surface in the product, so its parts are named instead of expressed as opacity math at call sites.
